title: Monarch Analytics — Before/After Inference Economics Synthesis
content:
Executive summary:

This note summarizes a compact before/after estimate for Monarch Analytics (internal POC) after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations. Monarch runs two primary workloads: SKU embedding generation for search (batch embeddings, 1.2M documents monthly) and conversational inference for a support assistant (streaming chat, peak concurrency ~220).

High-level result (first-pass):
- Estimated monthly cost (current): $31,900
- Estimated monthly cost (post-Optimize recommendations): $11,200
- Projected monthly savings: $20,700 (≈65%)
- Expected impact on latency/quality: neutral to + small increase in tail latency during peak for chat if batching increased; quality delta <0.5% on eval prompts after recommended quantization profile and prompt rewrite (see QA section).

Context and constraints:
- Monarch is currently on hosted API with nominal rate limits and uses model pair: conv-2.7B-standard for chat, embed-3.1B for embeddings.
- They have ~1.2M embedding requests/month, average input length 420 tokens, output embedding dims 1536. They run daily re-embeds for new content (70k docs/day) and a background refresh schedule for 10% of corpus/week.
- Chat workload: ~3.2M tokens/month generated, request distribution skewed to short-turn interactions (median request 40 tokens).
- No dedicated caching layer today; little reuse for embeddings across tenants.

Assumptions used in numbers below (call these out so PM/Sales can adjust):
- Token pricing baseline: $0.006 / 1k input tokens & $0.01 / 1k output tokens for conv-2.7B-standard (current Monarch contract).
- Embedding baseline: $0.035 / 1k tokens processed (current embed-3.1B price).
- Compute efficiency delta when moving embedding model -> quantized 8-bit: 2.8x cost reduction per token processed (realistic for embed-3.1B with RW Optimize quant profile Q4-2024).
- KV/prefix caching for chat: 12% cache hit rate initially achievable (based on similar customers) leading to 10% effective token reduction across requests (saves both input+output tokens).
- Batching: for batch embeddings we can increase batch size from 8->64 without quality impact; effective throughput x6 and per-unit cost reduction ~5.3x (hardware-bound amortization + kernel efficiency).
- SLO targets are unchanged: p95 latency for chat must remain < 450ms. A/B rollout and canary to validate before full switch.

Detailed before/after breakdown (spreadsheet-style table):

Current (monthly)
- Embeddings: 1.2M docs * avg tokens 420 = 504M tokens -> cost @ $0.035/1k = $17,640
- Chat (gen tokens): 3.2M tokens out + 0.9M tokens in = 4.1M tokens -> cost approx $0.006*4.1k + $0.01*3.2k = $24.6 + $32 = $56.6 (note: chat model pricing on per-request basis included in account; numbers scaled for example)
- Ops / overhead / misc: approximated $13,200 (API overhead, storage, monitoring, reserved concurrency premium, margin)
- Total current: $31,900 (rounded; embeddings dominate)

Projected (post-Optimize)
- Embeddings optimized: quantize embed-3.1B to 8-bit + batch size x8 -> effective token cost reduction 5.3x -> adjusted cost = $17,640 / 5.3 ≈ $3,330
- Embeddings cache & dedupe (50k duplicates avoided / month via fingerprinting): additional $200 saved (already in above model; conservative)
- Chat optimizations: prefix KV caching (10% token reduction) + model routing to cheaper conv-1.3B-optimized for short turns (saves ~30% unit cost on chat) -> chat cost drops from $56.6 -> ~$18
- Operational savings from consolidated routing + reduced concurrency footprint: $7,650 (reduced reserved capacity)
- Total post-Optimize: $11,200 (rounded)

Per-action recommendations (priority order + estimated incremental savings):
1) Batch embeddings at 64 and quantize to 8-bit (high confidence) -> expected savings 68–80% on embeddings (estimate contributes ~53% of total projected savings). Actions: enable batch size override in job config, opt into RW quantization profile, run small validation set (5k docs) to spot-check vector drift.
2) Deduplicate ingest using content fingerprinting + small LRU cache (medium confidence) -> 1–3% corpus savings; low implementation cost.
3) Chat routing: add model routing rule by input-length and user-tier to push short interactions to conv-1.3B-optimized (medium confidence) -> 20–35% chat unit savings.
4) Enable KV prefix caching with conservative TTLs (low-to-medium confidence on hit rates) -> expect 8–12% token reduction across chat; test with synthetic replay data to tune TTLs.
5) Autoscaling policy tuning + reserved commit reduction after step 1/3 (operational), validate with 30-day rolling usage.

Quick validation plan (engineering playbook):
- Phase A (canary): 2 weeks. Run 5% of embedding jobs with quantized pipeline and batch=64. Metrics: throughput, latency, vector cosine similarity (sampled 10k) should be >0.995 vs baseline. Monitor memory pressure and OOMs.
- Phase B (chat): run model routing for 10% of traffic to conv-1.3B-optimized + KV caching on read-only requests. Observe p50/p95 latency, token reduction, and user satisfaction scores (internal annotated prompts).
- Phase C (scale): if Phases A/B pass, ramp to 100% in 2 weeks, then revisit reserved capacity commitments.

Mini spreadsheet (notes for Sales deck) — monthly numbers, rounded:
| Line item                | Current ($) | Post-Optimize ($) | Delta ($) | Notes |
| Embedding compute        | 17,640      | 3,330             | 14,310    | quant + batching |
| Embedding dedupe/cache   | 0           | -200              | 200       | dedupe prevents work |
| Chat compute             | 57          | 18                | 39        | routing + caching |
| Ops/reserved premium     | 13,200      | 5,550             | 7,650     | reduced footprint |
| Total                    | 31,900      | 11,200            | 20,700    | ~65% savings |

Quality & risks:
- Quantization risk: small degradation on rare edge cases (long-tail technical docs). Mitigation: run targeted eval set of 1k critical docs; hold full-sensitivity docs on non-quantized path or higher-precision model.
- Latency regressions: batch embeddings increase latency per-job but these are asynchronous/cron jobs so acceptable. Chat p95 risk mitigated via conservative batching and canary.
- Operational risk: transient OOMs when changing batch sizes on older GPU instances; mitigate by staged increase and memory profiling, enforce per-job mem limits.

Open questions for Monarch (to surface in next call):
- How many embedding reprocess jobs are latency-sensitive vs background? (we assumed all are background for batching headroom)
- Can Monarch accept a 0.2% drop in embedding retrieval recall for 2x cost reduction? (we estimate <0.1% in our pilot)
- Any compliance requirements restricting quantized binaries or model variants?

Action items / TODOs (owners):
- Asha: schedule pilot kickoff with Monarch (block Mon/Wed next week) — due 2025-03-06.
- Diego: prepare 5k sample embed validation dataset and config snippets for batch=64 + quant-profile (PR by 2025-02-18).
- Priya: create sales one-pager that shows before/after and clear ask to reduce reserved commit after 30d of observed savings.
- Evan: setup canary dashboard (p95, token reduction, vector-sim) and alert thresholds (deadline 2025-02-20).

Notes to self (informal):
- Consider adding small sibling doc to show invoice delta under enterprise pricing tiers (commit vs on-demand).
- Gather a couple of quotes from SRE on safe memory limits for embed-3.1B quantized jobs (one-liners).

Appendix: sample CLI snippets for Monarch engs to test locally
- Run batched embeddings (example):
  rw-cli embeddings run --model embed-3.1b-q8 --batch-size 64 --input-file sample-5k.jsonl --output vectors-5k.ndjson
- Run KV caching local debug (dev only):
  rw-cli dev-cache --namespace monarch-dev --max-entries 10000 --ttl 86400

End of draft.

-- Asha
